newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks surge to record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks surge to record high at open.

text.p: Toronto stocks surged more than one percent to a new record high at the open on Thursday as investors on both sides of the border reacted positively to lower than expected U.S. jobs data.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 61.04 points to 6610.08 at the open before ticking up to a new high of 6615 in early trade.
The previous high was 6557, reached on June 16.
Trading volume was moderate as 9.3 million shares changed hands worth C$188.4 million. Advances outpaced declines 269 to 122, while 205 issues held steady.
Traders said the lower than expected U.S. jobs data, combined with the Fed's decision on Wednesday to leave rates unchanged, boosted market confidence that inflation remained at bay.

"You got all the interest-sensitive stocks running. The utility index is up close to two percent...that's what's providing the leadership. The rates just don't seem to be going anywhere at this particular time," one trader said.
All 14 of Toronto's sub-indexes gained ground, with utilities, banks, golds and industrials all rising more than one percent in early trade.
Traders said volume would taper off later in the session as U.S. investors headed out early for the long weekend. U.S. markets will be closed on Friday for Independence Day.
The U.S. Labor Department reported earlier today that payrolls rose by 217,000 in June compared to a revised 166,000 in May, while the unemployment rate ticked up to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent.
Analysts had expected June non-farm payrolls to rise by about 222,000 and the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.8 percent.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* Banks stocks led the morning rally. Shares in Bank of Nova Scotia and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose 1.10 to 63.60 and 36.95, respectively, while shares in Royal Bank of Canada rose 0.90 to 65.75.
((Andrea Hopkins at Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8102 or e-mail andrea.hopkins@reuters.com))

Interest-sensitive issues such as banks and utilities extended Wednesday's rally of relief after the U.S. Federal Reserve left short-term interest rates untouched.
"I don't see any black clouds on the horizon that could hurt the market," a trader said.
Trading was moderate at 90 million shares worth C$1.7 billion.

Only four of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors sagged, led by golds and forestry products. The influential gold group shed almost 2.5 percent, dragged down by the key Comex bullion price, which closed $7.10 lower at $325.20.
